canonical_title: Exterior field of view - Air vehicles with single or tandem pilots
subject_group: 9.4.4 External visibility and transmitted visual indications

versions.title_at_revision: Exterior field of view - Air vehicles with single or tandem pilots
versions.text:
Standard: No windscreen structure forward of the canopy bow exceeds 2.0 inches in width when projected onto a plane perpendicular to a line between the structure and the design eye position. The blind spot caused by the structure between the top of the windscreen and the canopy does not exceed 35 degrees horizontally nor 7 degrees vertically. The following minimum angles of unimpaired vision are available to the pilot in the forward position, from the design eye positions shown in TABLE XI. TABLE XI. Exterior FOV - Air vehicles with single or tandem pilots - forward position. At 0° azimuth, 11° down and 10° up. At 20° azimuth, left and right, 20° down. At 30° azimuth, left and right, 25° down. At 90° azimuth, left and right, 40° down. At 135° azimuth, left and right, 20° down. For the aft position, at 20 degrees azimuth, a minimum of 5 degrees vision down is provided, measured from the aft design eye box with the forward seat in the neutral seat position. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analyze vision plots and verify that the total envelope (plus and minus 180 degrees in azimuth and plus and minus 90 degrees in elevation) from each pilot’s design eye box provides the required clear vision areas required by the standard. Vision plots are completed for each pilot’s position for all their primary operations. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
  (1) Demonstrate in flight that the external FOV allows the pilots to perform all their primary operations.
